provenance.instrument: Middlesex Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 175 Zoning, Ord. No. 21 of 10-7-1992, amended in its entirety by Ord. No. 108 of 9-20-2006, as amended), with Chapter 84 Floodplain Management (Ord. No. 132 of 6-20-2018), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 MI2094, Township of Middlesex, PA. 175-8 defines 'County' as the 'County of Butler, Pennsylvania', so this is Middlesex township, Butler County. Middlesex Township in Cumberland County is a different place. Each district article sets its uses and figures in text, and the chapter has no attachments. The ADU text was added by Ord. No. 138 of 12-20-2023, and the latest amendment seen is Ord. No. 140 of 10-16-2024
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows 'Includes legislation through 10-16-2024.' New Laws lists only Ord. No. 141 of 1-21-2026 (salaries)
checks: Accessory dwelling units are a use by special exception, as an accessory use, in AG-A, AG-B, R-1, R-2 and R-AG (175-14C(2)(f), 175-21C(2)(f), 175-28C(2)(c), 175-200C(2)(b), 175-244C(2)(f)), under 175-95.1 (Ord. No. 138 of 12-20-2023). The use lists of C-1, C-2, I-1, TC, C-3 and the Route 228 corridor overlay were read: none lists an ADU. C-1, C-2, I-1 and C-3 list no dwelling but a temporary dwelling, a group care facility or transitional dwelling and a home occupation. TC permits garden apartments, single-family dwellings, townhouses and two-family dwellings by right (175-210A). The Route 228 overlay lists single-family dwellings, townhouses and planned residential development

An accessory dwelling unit is 'A secondary dwelling unit established in conjunction with and clearly subordinate to a primary dwelling unit, whether a part of the same structure as the primary dwelling unit or a detached dwelling unit on the same lot'. A granny flat, carriage house or in-law suite is an ADU with its own entrance, kitchen, bathroom and living area, often above a rear detached garage, attached to the house at grade or detached (175-8). 175-95.1A permits the unit 'as an accessory structure to a primary residence', and an accessory structure is detached from the principal building (175-8)

175-95.1: one ADU per lot, at least 400 sq ft of gross floor area, at most 1,200 sq ft or 50% of the total square footage of the primary dwelling unit, whichever is less, DEP on-lot sewage rules where they apply, and the district's setback and area and bulk rules. The code sets no owner-occupancy, family or rental rule for the unit. Short-term rentals are a separate special exception

Special exceptions: the Zoning Hearing Board after a hearing, with written notice to owners within 450 ft, on an application with a land development plan (boundary survey, contours, yards, parking layout), the general standards of 175-94 (performance standards, parking, screening, steep slopes, storage, safe access) and approval lapsing after six months without a permit application (175-93, 175-94, 175-176)

Accessory buildings 'shall not be permitted in the required front yard or required side yards', meet the district rear yard for accessory structures and stand at least 5 ft from any principal building, though a detached garage may be joined to the house (175-142C(7)). Accessory structures: rear 10 ft in every district read and side 10 ft in AG-A, AG-B and R-AG, height 15 ft (25 ft on two acres or more in AG-A, AG-B and R-AG, one story in R-2) (175-15, 175-22, 175-29, 175-201, 175-245). In R-2 private garages and sheds are permitted only on a lot with a single-family dwelling (175-200A(2)(a)). A unit over a garage is a second story, but R-2 accessory structures are '15 feet or one story' (175-201G(2)), so a unit over a garage cannot be built in R-2, and on a lot under two acres elsewhere the 15 ft cap leaves little room for one

Lot coverage is the share of the lot 'covered by all principal and accessory structures' (175-8): 20% in AG-A, AG-B and R-AG (5% for farms), 35% in R-1, 45% in R-2. Land over 25% slope counts toward neither lot area nor coverage, and no building may stand on it (175-141)

Parking: 2 spaces per single-family or two-family dwelling unit, and for an ADU '1 off-street space, in addition to the spaces required for the primary dwelling unit', in an enclosed garage or a private driveway on the lot. Any fraction of a space counts as one (175-156A(5)(a), B(1), B(5) Table 3). A conversion apartment needs 'One off-street parking space ... for each dwelling unit' (175-106F), but Table 3 asks 2 per dwelling unit for single-family and two-family dwellings, so 4 spaces on the stricter reading

Floodplain (Chapter 84, FIRM of August 2, 2018): new construction and substantial improvements of residential structures are elevated to the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. In the floodway nothing may raise flood levels and new construction needs a DEP permit, and in an AE area without a floodway nothing new within 50 ft of the top of bank without a DEP permit. Manufactured homes are barred from the floodway and from 50 ft of the top of bank. Chapter 84 sets no separate rule for accessory structures. The Zoning Hearing Board hears floodplain variances (84-17, 84-19, 84-24, 84-28, 84-32 to 84-34, 175-174E). Hospitals, nursing homes, jails, landfills, cemeteries and some other activities are prohibited in the floodplain (84-30). None is a dwelling

Nonconforming lots: a lot of record in separate ownership may be built on below the minimum lot area and width if it meets the yards, height and lot coverage (175-169A). A nonconforming use may be enlarged by special exception (175-167B)

Variances go to the Zoning Hearing Board on the MPC findings (175-175). No bar on a use variance was found. 'Any use not expressly listed for a zoning district is not permitted in that district', unless the Zoning Hearing Board authorizes it as a comparable use where the district lists comparable uses by special exception (175-12A, 175-105). Those districts are C-1, C-2, I-1, TC and C-3. AG-A, AG-B, R-1, R-2 and R-AG do not list them

Temporary dwellings are permitted only during construction with the Board of Supervisors' permission (175-147). A planned residential development is a conditional use in R-1, R-2 and R-AG under Article X, which was not read

In AG-A, AG-B and R-AG farm buildings may share a lot with a single-family dwelling, but 'Two single-family dwellings shall not occupy the same lot unless all applicable requirements of the Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance are met' (175-12C). In R-1 'a single-family dwelling or two-family dwelling shall be the only principal structure on the lot. All dwelling units shall be located within the same principal structure' (175-12D)

R-2 also permits garden apartments, quad-plexes and townhouses by right, on 43,560 sq ft for 'All other uses' (175-200A(1), 175-201A(3)). A family includes 'No more than four unrelated individuals occupying a premises and living as single housekeeping unit' (175-8)

Accessory height: on a lot of two acres or more in AG-A, AG-B and R-AG accessory structures may be 25 ft (175-15I(2)(b), 175-22I(2)(b), 175-245I(2)(b)). The tool still shows the 15 ft cap on such a lot, with the 25 ft as a condition

Side yards for the unit: 175-95.1A sends the unit to 'all applicable setback ... requirements of the zoning district'. AG-A, AG-B and R-AG give 'Dwellings: 25 feet each side' and 'Accessory structures: 10 feet each side', and the unit is both. R-2 gives 10 ft for a single-family dwelling and 'All other uses: 15 feet each side'. R-1 sets side yards for principal structures only. The code does not settle which side yard binds the unit

value.name: Conversion apartment (AG-A, AG-B, R-1, R-2, R-AG)
value.conditions: A conversion apartment is 'A dwelling unit, as defined herein, established within an existing single-family dwelling', a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in each of these districts. Each dwelling unit has at least 900 sq ft of gross floor area and its own living, sleeping, kitchen and sanitary facilities, at most two units in the building, no conversion of a basement, garage or other accessory structure, safe ingress and egress and a turnaround on the lot, one off-street space per dwelling unit (Table 3 asks 2 per dwelling unit for single-family and two-family dwellings, so 4 spaces on the stricter reading), and Department of Labor and Industry rules. The general special exception standards of 175-94 and the application with a land development plan of 175-93 apply

requires.condition: Each of the two units needs at least 900 sq ft of gross floor area, so the house needs at least 1,800 sq ft

value.note: The 1,800 sq ft house test is read from the 900 sq ft per unit minimum. The code sets no lot area for the conversion

value.name: Two-family dwelling (AG-A, R-AG)
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling, 'two independent dwelling units, each having a separate entrance', and 'the only principal building on the lot', is permitted by right. The lot needs 1.5 acres with both public water and public sewage, 2 acres without either, and 175 ft of width. Side yards 25 ft each, rear 75 ft. Two spaces per dwelling unit

min_lot_by_utility.when: With both public water and public sewage

value.note: A building that becomes two units by conversion of an existing house is the conversion apartment listing, by special exception

value.name: Two-family dwelling (AG-B, R-1, R-2)
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling, the only principal building on the lot, with a separate entrance for each unit, is permitted by right. The lot needs 2 acres in AG-B, one acre and 150 ft of width in R-1, and 21,780 sq ft and 100 ft of width in R-2. Side yards 25 ft each in AG-B and R-1, 15 ft each in R-2. Two spaces per dwelling unit
value.note: A building that becomes two units by conversion of an existing house is the conversion apartment listing, by special exception

value.name: Two-family dwelling (TC)
value.conditions: TC permits two-family dwellings by right. A two-family dwelling has 'two independent dwelling units, each having a separate entrance', and is 'the only principal building on the lot'. The lot needs 8,000 sq ft and 80 ft of width, lot coverage at most 75%, a front yard of 20 ft (35 ft on an arterial street) and at most 85 ft, side yards of 10 ft (15 ft next to an AG or R district), a rear yard of 20 ft, and accessory structures 5 ft from the rear line and at most 15 ft or one story. No residential use within 150 ft of an arterial street right-of-way. Two spaces per dwelling unit
value.note: TC lists no conversion apartment, so whether an existing house may become a two-family dwelling is not settled. Ask the zoning officer

value.condition: In R-1 'a single-family dwelling or two-family dwelling shall be the only principal structure on the lot', and all dwelling units are located within the same principal structure. A unit in a detached building is a dwelling unit outside the house.

disputed_by.note: 175-95.1, added in 2023, permits the unit in R-1 'as an accessory structure to a primary residence'. The later and more specific rule may govern, so a detached unit may be allowed

value.condition: Land with a natural or finished slope over 25% 'shall not be used for the construction of any principal or accessory building', grading or construction on slopes over 40% is not permitted, and land over 25% is left out of the lot area and lot coverage figures. A special exception must meet the steep slope rules.

'When applicable, accessory dwelling units shall meet Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) requirements for on-lot sewage facilities.' A unit served by public sewer is not reached by this rule.

In the identified floodplain any new construction or substantial improvement of a residential structure has its lowest floor, basement included, at or above the regulatory flood elevation, the base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft. No expansion may raise the base flood elevation in the floodway, or more than one foot with other development in an AE area without a floodway. Work of 50% or more of market value must fully comply. New construction is a structure begun on or after the chapter's effective date (Ord. No. 132 of 6-20-2018), with its later improvements. The Zoning Hearing Board hears floodplain variances.

In the floodway no encroachment is permitted unless it causes no increase in flood levels, no new construction or development without a DEP permit, and no manufactured home. No variance may raise the base flood elevation there.

In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection regional office.' No manufactured home may stand within 50 ft of the top of bank anywhere in the identified floodplain.

The side yard shown for a unit in an accessory building is the 10 ft for accessory structures. The unit is also a dwelling, and the district gives 'Dwellings: 25 feet each side'. The code does not settle which holds, and 25 ft is the safe reading.

The side yard shown for a unit in an accessory building is the 10 ft for a single-family dwelling. Read under 'All other uses: 15 feet each side' it is 15 ft. The code does not settle which holds, and 15 ft is the safe reading.
In R-2 accessory structures are at most 15 ft or one story, and the unit is an accessory structure. A unit over a garage is a second story, so it cannot be built there.
